hook: Which city wastes more water: one that uses 200 million liters a day, or one that uses 20 million? You cannot tell until you know how many people live in each. Dividing a total by the number of people, the area or the time turns raw totals into rates you can compare fairly, and the exam asks for them constantly.

prereq.why: Divide the fronts (3.0) and subtract the exponents (7 - 3 = 4).

prereq.q: Which reservoir holds most of Earth’s freshwater that is not ice?
prereq.why: Groundwater holds far more than lakes, rivers and the air.

figure.caption: The bigger total is not always the bigger amount per person.

chain.cause: Divide a total by the number of people
Divide by an area or a time instead
chain.effect: you get a density or a rate per unit of time

chain.cause: Keep the units in the setup
chain.effect: the answer’s unit tells you what you found: L per person, people per km²

ideas: A rate compares two quantities with different units: liters per day, people per km², kg per person.
A unit rate is a rate for one unit of the second quantity: 150 L per 1 person.
Per capita means per person: the total ÷ the population.
The word after "per" goes on the bottom: liters per km = L ÷ km.

misconception.wrong: The place with the biggest total uses resources the most heavily.
misconception.right: Big totals often just mean more people. Divide by the population (per capita) before you decide who uses more.

summary: A rate divides one quantity by another: liters per day, people per km², kilograms per person. A per-capita value divides a total by the number of people, so places of different sizes can be compared fairly. Write the setup with units: the word after "per" goes on the bottom, and the units of the answer tell you what you found.
